scams.name: The Catania Fontanarossa Airport Taxi Overcharge to Taormina
scams.description: Unlicensed and discretionary-pricing drivers quote €150–€250 for the 55km Catania Fontanarossa to Taormina run against a regulated €90–€100 zone fare. A TripAdvisor Sicily forum topic 'Watch out for official taxi scams from Catania Airport' documents a driver who dropped from €250 to €185 and then €135 when the hotel concierge intervened. A May 18, 2025 LiveSicilia report documents Catania police sanctioning four unlicensed 'tassisti abusivi' at the airport in a single enforcement action. A separate TripAdvisor review 'Rip off taxi' documents paying €30 for a 7-minute ride that should have been €18 fixed.
scams.avoidance: Take the Alibus city bus (€1.50) to Catania Centrale then Interbus to Taormina (~€5.10, ~75 minutes) — €6.60 total versus a €90+ taxi. If you must use a taxi, use only vehicles at the signed official rank outside Arrivals, confirm the €90–€100 zone fare before closing the door, and ask for 'tariffa concordata' in writing on the ricevuta. Pre-book a licensed NCC with a quoted fixed fare (€85–€110 with receipt). Demand a receipt with taxi number, time, route, and total.
scams.location: Catania Fontanarossa Airport (CTA) taxi rank and arrivals forecourt; Via Pirandello taxi rank in Taormina

scams.name: The Teatro Antico "Skip-the-Line" Ticket Markup
scams.description: The Teatro Antico di Taormina official price is €14 intero / €7 ridotto at the Sicilia Region archaeological gate (parchiarcheologici.regione.sicilia.it). Third-party resellers on Corso Umberto bundle the same entry at €24–€26 as 'skip the line' or 'guided' — sicilia.info, City Sightseeing, Tiqets and Musement all list €24+ packages. A May 20, 2025 Gazzetta del Sud cronaca ('Taormina, i turisti pagano il biglietto al Teatro Antico ma dentro trovano impalcature e teli') documented tourists with pre-paid tour tickets arriving to find scaffolding and tarps inside, with no refund offered. A TripAdvisor 'BEWARE! A SCAM' review of Sicily Excursions by Noema Viaggi flags day-tour packages that list Teatro Antico but reduce the visit to minutes.
scams.avoidance: Buy at the on-site box office at Via Teatro Greco 1 or on parchiarcheologici.regione.sicilia.it / aditusculture.com — always €14 intero / €7 ridotto, free the first Sunday of every month and for EU residents under 18. If scaffolding is visible from outside, ask what percentage of the theater is under restoration before paying. Only 'skip-the-line' through refundable platforms (GetYourGuide, Tiqets, Headout). Always pay by card for chargeback recourse.
scams.location: Via Teatro Greco (Teatro Antico approach), Corso Umberto ticket booths, Piazza IX Aprile and Piazza Vittorio Emanuele tour kiosks

scams.name: The Isola Bella Fake-Ticket & "Beach Massage" Hustle
scams.description: Isola Bella is a WWF-managed nature reserve charging €5 intero / €2.50 ridotto (per the April 2024 98zero.com reopening notice) — or €6/€3 in some seasons via traveltaormina.com, with €1 Messina-province-resident rate. A Facebook 'Vacanze in Sicilia' post documents a tourist being scammed out of €1,000 by a fake 'resident' ticket reseller. A TripAdvisor 'Beware the massage scam' review documents Asian women working together to impose unquoted €40–€80 'massage' fees on beach-goers after offering a 'free' sample — the same MO runs at Mondello (Palermo) and other Sicilian beaches.
scams.avoidance: Pay only at the Isola Bella causeway booth (WWF/Comune) — €5 intero / €2.50 ridotto, printed ticket with date and barcode. Refuse any roaming massage, 'sample', or bracelet with a firm 'no grazie' — physical contact is the charge cue. Use the funivia (€3/€6) rather than the stairs if mobility is a concern, and buy funivia tickets only at the funivia booth. Carry only €40–€60 cash to the beach.
scams.location: Isola Bella nature reserve and causeway (below funivia lower station, accessed by stair-descent from Via Luigi Pirandello)

scams.name: Mount Etna Unlicensed Guide & Summit-Access Scam
scams.description: Unlicensed 'Etna tours' sell 'summit access' that legally requires a certified Guida Alpina Vulcanologica dell'Etna above 2,500m. A November 21, 2017 Catania Today report (confirmed by Bronte118 and Euroetnatourism) documents a Guardia di Finanza soccorso alpino operation that stopped a group of 15 tourists being led toward the summit by an unlicensed guide, with the operator denounced to the Procura di Catania for 'esercizio abusivo della professione.' Codacons Sicilia's February 2025 advisory reiterates the authorization rule. A March 12, 2025 TripAdvisor review of a major Catania-based Etna tour operator flags 'Scam company beware — highly unethical refund policy and no customer support,' and community traveler threads repeatedly warn 'Mt. Etna tours are a scam.'
scams.avoidance: Book only through a Guida Alpina Vulcanologica Etna listed at guidevulcanologichenord.it or guidetnasud.com with a verifiable license number. For DIY, take AST bus 457 from Catania Centrale (€6.60 return) to Rifugio Sapienza; the funivia dell'Etna reaches 2,500m (€50) and certified guides to the summit are €75 per person. Refuse quad/ATV pitches without ENIT registration and published polizza RC insurance. Always pay by credit card.
scams.location: Rifugio Sapienza (Etna south base, 1,900m), Piano Provenzana (north base); pickup at Via Pirandello and Piazza Sant'Antonio in Taormina, also Giardini Naxos and Catania

scams.name: The Corso Umberto "Pesce al Etto" Restaurant Trap
scams.description: Corso Umberto restaurants layer three mechanisms: €3–€5 per-person coperto (often unposted), 10–15% automatic 'servizio' applied only to foreign-card totals, and pesce/carne 'al etto' (per 100g) that turns a headline €8 sea bass into a €48–€64 receipt. An Italian-language TripAdvisor review of a Corso Umberto restaurant names it: 'tre euro di coperto e i prezzi esagerati perché siamo a Taormina.' Traveler reports call the town 'an absolute tourist trap... sky high prices for everything' and advise 'Skip the Corso Umberto at peak hours. Between 11:00 and 18:00 it becomes a catwalk.'
scams.avoidance: Walk 3–5 minutes off Corso Umberto — Via Bagnoli Croce, Via Pirandello, or the Castelmola road yield real Sicilian trattorie. Photograph the posted outside menu before sitting (Italian law requires prices). Ask the waiter to weigh the fish at the table and confirm the total. Ask 'mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?' at sit-down. Trust Italian-language Most-Recent Google reviews over English ones.
scams.location: Corso Umberto (800m pedestrian strip), Piazza IX Aprile café terraces, Piazza Vittorio Emanuele

scams.name: Mazzarò & Spisone Lido Minimum-Spend Ambush
scams.description: Taormina's private lidi (Lido Mazzarò, Lido La Pigna, Lido Caparena, Spisone/Mazzeo clubs) layer undisclosed per-lounger rates (€40/lounger × 2 plus umbrella), mandatory F&B minimums of €20–€40 per person, and first-row-versus-second-row surcharges not announced until departure. TripAdvisor reviewers put it plainly: 'Most of the beach is private with sun beds at cost. The public bit is small with limited access.' Community guides warn Isola Bella and Mazzarò require long staircases that prime tired visitors to accept the first lido offer. Italian Codice del Consumo requires pre-purchase disclosure of minimums — Italian-only signs and verbal pitches are the enforcement loophole.
scams.avoidance: Ask for the lido's day-rate price list in writing (prezzo giornaliero, lettino, ombrellone, F&B minimum) before sitting down. Pack towels and use the free spiaggia libera — every Mazzarò and Spisone bay has a public strip marked by a small blue concrete sign. Consider Spisone or Mazzeo (cheaper lidi ~€15/lounger, 20 minutes north). Pay by credit card for chargeback recourse. If a lido enforces an undisclosed minimum, refuse, photograph the bill, and call Polizia Municipale di Taormina.
scams.location: Lido Mazzarò, Lido La Pigna, Lido Caparena, Spisone/Mazzeo beach clubs (reached from funivia lower station and Via Nazionale SS114)

scams.name: The Fake Day-Tour & Hotel-Transfer Scam
scams.description: Taormina 'Sicily highlights' day tours and 'free' hotel-airport transfers collapse on arrival day — itineraries swap to shopping routes, Taormina time drops to 20 minutes, or the 'free' transfer disappears with €30 per person extracted at check-out. TripAdvisor 'BEWARE! A SCAM' for Sicily Excursions by Noema Viaggi, a 'SCAM — they will steal your money' review of Viaggiare car rental, and the August 2023 'Scammed out of €300' Taormina Park Hotel review all document the same non-refundable, non-responsive pattern. Wonderful Italy Experiences Sicily carries a 'SCAM! STAY AWAY' review documenting a Palermo stay cancelled two hours before arrival with no refund. A Facebook Sicilia post catalogues the 'Cambio di Programma' bait-and-switch.
scams.avoidance: Book only through GetYourGuide, Viator, Tiqets, or Musement — platform-backed refunds matter more than the specific operator. Sort platform reviews by Most Recent and read 2- and 3-stars for specific swap patterns. Confirm airport transfers in writing in the hotel reservation email (not verbally in the lobby). Always pay by credit card. If scammed, file with the platform, ENIT-Italia, and Comune di Taormina Polizia Municipale.
scams.location: Tour-operator kiosks on Corso Umberto, Piazza IX Aprile and Piazza Vittorio Emanuele; online listings targeting Taormina Park Hotel and Giardini Naxos resort guests
